text: 📸 Mañanera del Pueblo — Coatzacoalcos, Veracruz · 5 de junio de 2026

🇲🇽🏭 190 billion pesos for Veracruz over the term. Plus 79 billion a year in Bienestar programs. "It is an investment in Veracruz of around 190 billion pesos over the six-year term — petrochemicals and fertilizers, highways, drinking water, treatment plants, river recovery, and health. Plus Bienestar programs reaching close to 79 billion pesos in a single year. A historic investment for Veracruz." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera in Coatzacoalcos Fourteenth presidential visit to Veracruz in less than a year. Governor Rocío Nahle — former Energy Minister — runs the state where PEMEX's petrochemical heart sits. Pairs heavy industrial reactivation with welfare-state expansion in the same budget line.

🇲🇽🚆 Mexico is rebuilding bridges to survive 1,000-year storms. "We are already designing for thousand-year return periods, for thousand-year rainfall events." — Jesús Esteva, Infrastructure Secretary 18 bridges being intervened in Veracruz alone: 11 new builds, 6 expansions, 1 rehabilitation. After the October 2024 floods that battered the Huasteca, infrastructure design standards were rewritten upward — climate-resilient by default, not retrofitted.

🇲🇽🚆 Coatzacoalcos III will be the longest and tallest bridge of Sheinbaum's term — built over water. "It will surely be the longest and tallest bridge we will build in this administration. And also, over a body of water." — Jesús Esteva, Infrastructure Secretary Coatzacoalcos III: 6 km total length, 40 meters high, main span 200 meters, cable-stayed (atirantado). Bidding documents went out yesterday; construction starts July 2026, finishes in three years. Lets large-draft ships pass through the port.

🇲🇽🌎 Mahahual blocks mega-tourism. A decree restricts the Costa Maya zone to eco-tourism with the community. "The objective is to give it a protected status so that only ecotourism can be developed there. This can only be done together with the community." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera in Coatzacoalcos — World Environment Day Mahahual, in southern Quintana Roo, was lined up for a large-scale tourism project. The federal government, Semarnat, Sectur, Fonatur and the state will sign a decree to protect the area for community-led ecotourism. Quintana Roo confirmed 197.5 million pesos for local infrastructure. Announced from Holbox alongside the México Circular plan against single-use plastics.

🇲🇽✊ After 25 years of demands, La Montaña de Guerrero finally gets its hospital. "After more than 25 years of demands and just struggle by the community, there is now certainty that this hospital will be built." — Alejandro Svarch, IMSS Bienestar director Atlixtac sits in La Montaña, one of the most marginalized regions in Mexico. The new hospital will have 31 beds, urgencias, surgery, imaging, pediatrics, gynecology — and traditional medicine, because, in Svarch's words, "La Montaña has knowledge that the public system has an obligation to respect." Construction starts this year.

🇲🇽✊ 98% oncology drug stock — the highest ever recorded in Mexico's public hospitals. "We have 98 percent oncology drug supply in the state — a number never before reached, which guarantees no cancer patient at any of the five IMSS Bienestar oncology hospitals in Veracruz will lose continuity of treatment." — Alejandro Svarch, IMSS Bienestar director, mañanera in Coatzacoalcos Veracruz is on track for 5 million free consultations in 2026 — a million more than last year, a record for the state. 22 million medicine units already delivered. 734 health centers will get internet, electronic medical records, and on-site labs in the next three months. 100% free.

🇲🇽🛢️ PEMEX is reviving the petrochemical industry Mexico abandoned to imports. "For decades, in our country, the petrochemical industry was abandoned, making us dependent on imports — wasting the chance to multiply the value of our hydrocarbons." — Juan Carlos Carpio, PEMEX director, mañanera in Coatzacoalcos Today PEMEX presented a 93-billion-peso plan (2026–2030) to reactivate petrochemicals and fertilizers at the Cangrejera, Morelos, Cosoleacaque, ProAgro and Fertinal complexes. Target: 849,000 tons/year of petrochemicals and 4 million tons of fertilizers — feeding the food-sovereignty agenda. New Escolín plant alone is 25 billion pesos.

🇲🇽📊 <u>WALL STREET ANALYSTS CUT MEXICO GDP TO 1.10% — THIRD STRAIGHT DOWNWARD REVISION</u>

Banxico's May survey (released June 1) of 43 private-sector firms cut their 2026 GDP forecast to 1.10% from 1.38%, and pegged year-end inflation at 4.35%. Forty-two percent of analysts named "governance" as the top obstacle — Wall Street code for "Sheinbaum keeps regulating us."

Same crew that has been wrong all year about Mexico's recession that never came, the peso collapse that never came, and the nearshoring "death" that didn't happen either.

Meanwhile reinvestment of profits in Mexico jumped 33.5% in Q1 — the only data that matters comes from capital that's already here.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>WORLD BANK RULES UNANIMOUSLY FOR MEXICO — US MINER OWES $998K AFTER LOSING $315M CLAIM</u>

ICSID — the World Bank's investment arbitration tribunal — unanimously dismissed Silver Bull Resources' $315 million NAFTA claim against Mexico on May 29, 2026. The US miner had sued in 2023 after a local mining cooperative in Sierra Mojada, Coahuila blocked its concessions starting September 2019.

The tribunal ruled it had no jurisdiction, that the alleged facts fell outside NAFTA's time window, and ordered Silver Bull to pay Mexico ~$998,000 USD in legal costs.

Foreign mining capital tried investor-state arbitration as a weapon against communities defending their land. It lost — and had to pay for the privilege.
